silo_relevance: This paper is highly relevant to portfolio_optimization because it maps core allocation problems—mean-variance, CVaR, and Sharpe-ratio optimization—into conic feasibility forms that can be attacked by multiplicative-weights solvers. Its main portfolio-specific value is showing when these models are LP/SOCP/SDP-representable and how the Sharpe-ratio case can be reduced to SOCP feasibility via bisection.

key_points.point: Portfolio construction problems are organized into LP/SOCP/SDP forms, giving a direct modeling route for allocation and risk-control tasks.
key_points.silo_note: For portfolio_optimization, the key issue is whether a desired objective or risk constraint can be expressed in a solver-friendly conic form; this paper provides that mapping for several standard portfolio models.

key_points.point: Sharpe-ratio portfolio optimization is reduced to SOCP feasibility and then solved by bisection, which is a concrete portfolio-specific reduction.
key_points.silo_note: Sharpe ratio is a central portfolio selection objective, so the ability to convert it into repeated feasibility checks is directly useful for optimization workflows.

key_points.point: The SOCP-specific MW algorithm is especially relevant because it targets the cone structure that appears in portfolio models, rather than relying on a generic SDP embedding.
key_points.silo_note: For portfolio_optimization, preserving SOCP structure matters because it can make the solver more aligned with the problem formulation and avoid losing efficiency in a denser SDP reformulation.

key_points.point: The paper highlights practical portfolio data structure—factor-structured covariance matrices and whitening/equilibration—which affects convergence and data access.
key_points.silo_note: In portfolio_optimization, covariance structure is central to mean-variance and related allocation problems, so these observations matter for how the algorithm scales on realistic inputs.

key_points.point: Cardinality-constrained portfolio optimization is flagged as NP-hard, with mixed-integer solvers often practical at moderate sizes, limiting the reach of the conic/MW approach for sparse portfolios.
key_points.silo_note: Sparse portfolio selection is a major portfolio_optimization variant, and this paper’s caveat is important because it shows where the proposed framework may not be the best practical tool.
